You are making Cyrus's build capacity launch-ready on branch `feature/cyrus-capacity-queue`, worktree `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-capacity` (git repo of /opt/nxeon, from release/cyrus-rc8 916eb4fb20; work ONLY there). Read first: /root/CLAUDE.md, /root/claudeskills/agent-notes/HANDOFF-FULL.md (section 5b), CYRUS-TRACKER.md sections 97, 101, 103 (agent-notes/cyrus-research), docs/cyrus/07-operations.md, docs/CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md, services/modbuilder/{server.js,run.sh,usage.js,live.js}, lib/cyrus/builder/*, lib/modbuilder/*, lib/cyrus/tokens/spend.ts, lib/cyrus/planner/*, components/cyrus/prompt/* (cost/wait wording), app/admin/cyrus/builds + live.

PROBLEM (measured/observed 2026-10-13/14): one build VM (88001, container 5 GB, MB_CONCURRENCY=2). The owner's interactive build waited behind two eval builds ("there should be no queue"). The subscription login hit its session limit when agents and evals ran at the same time. Public launch needs predictable waits, fairness between accounts, and protection of interactive users from batch work, without a second paid VM being mandatory on day one.

DELIVER (commit per part; all behind default-safe settings):
1. PRIORITY CLASSES in the build service: `interactive` (portal user builds), `batch` (eval, mining jobs, admin re-runs), `system` (guard/planner/health). Reserve capacity: batch may never occupy the last interactive slot (configurable MB_RESERVE_INTERACTIVE, default 1 of MB_CONCURRENCY); queue ordering = priority, then per-account fair share (round robin by userId), then FIFO; starvation guard for batch. Request field `priority` (+ an `eval:` id-prefix fallback so existing eval runner sets batch automatically). Backwards compatible API.
2. CAPACITY KNOBS and safety: derive safe MB_CONCURRENCY from container memory/CPU (document the measured per-build RSS from /var/lib/modbuilder data and the Test Flight/javac footprint), admission control with an honest queue position and estimated wait (p50/p80 from recent durations), per-account concurrent-build cap (setting, default 2) and rate limits that return a clear retryable error; graceful degradation when the AI backend answers ai_unavailable/rate-limited (no charge, automatic retry with backoff and a plain message, circuit breaker so a limit hit does not fail a whole queue).
3. PORTAL: plan/build screens show queue position and expected wait truthfully (no fake ETAs), "starting soon" vs "waiting for a free builder", and a calm retry message on capacity or AI-unavailable; token holds are released on refusal (existing ledger rules); admin Live tab shows queue depth, wait percentiles, concurrency and the priority mix, with an alert threshold setting.
4. SCALE-OUT READINESS (no new paid VM is created by you): the service can be pointed at N build workers: write the design + minimal implementation of a stateless dispatcher mode (portal chooses among MODBUILDER_URLS by load from /health, sticky per build id) and a runbook to add a second build VM (docs only for the VM steps: image, env, key, firewall via node-2, `deploy-modbuilder.sh` V/JUMP vars). Implement the portal-side multi-worker selection behind a setting (default single worker) with tests using fakes.
5. LOAD TEST with fakes: extend the fake CLI/service tests to simulate 3 accounts x 5 builds + 10 batch builds: assert interactive wait bounded, fairness, reservation, no starvation, correct queue positions. Optionally a small `scripts/cyrus/queue-sim.ts` that prints the distribution.

RULES: never build/run in /opt/nxeon; heavy commands only via `/opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost` from inside the worktree (`devhost tsc`, `devhost test <files>`, `devhost run -- ...`, `devhost build`, `devhost db push` throwaway DB; node-2's build lock is shared: never hold it longer than needed, never two locked jobs at once). If a call is denied by the permission classifier, do NOT retry or work around it: note it in the report. No production actions: no deploys, no image redeploy, no env/flag/setting writes in prod, no VM writes, no paid model calls. New files under services/modbuilder must be in the Dockerfile COPY list (test checks). DB: additive manual SQL only, NOT applied. Stage explicit paths, never `git add -A` at repo root. Commit with trailer `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>`. Docs: docs-build + rsync generated refs from root@178.63.94.114:/tank/nxeon-build/wt/cyrus-capacity/ (and build-*-artifacts for bundled validators). Warn-don't-block applies to user choices; capacity/security/money limits stay hard.

FINISH: `devhost tsc` = 0; full suite green (`devhost test test/cyrus-*.test.ts test/modbuilder-*.test.ts test/mods-*.test.ts`; cyrus-admin flake alone); docs 07/09/11/12 + CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK updated. Final report under 220 words: commits, tests, defaults chosen (PLACEHOLDER marked), what needs an image redeploy vs a portal promote, how the owner enables it, unverified items.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type parameter to select which agent type to use. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

tools.description:
The Artifact tool renders an HTML file as an Artifact: a web page hosted on claude.ai that is private by default. Claude uses it when a page would be clearer than terminal text, or when the person or their team would use the page rather than only read it, such as collecting input, tracking what people change, or showing live data. Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. The exception is content that could mislead or cause harm if shared further: anything that imitates a real organization, person or record, and anything the person presented as sensitive. action.description: One of 'publish', 'list', 'read', 'delete', 'pin', 'unpin'. Omitting it means 'publish'. **Calls** in the description says what each one does and takes, except as noted here.

file_path.description: publish: the local page Claude publishes (.html, or .md only when a skill says so). With `asset: true`, it is the local file Claude uploads. A short, distinctive basename also serves as the title when nothing else gives one.

asset.description: publish with `url`: true uploads `file_path` (or each of `file_paths`) to that artifact's asset store instead of publishing it as the page (see **Calls**).

file_paths.description: publish with `asset: true` only: several local image, video, PDF, font, stylesheet or script files in place of `file_path`, up to 25 in one call, all into the artifact that `url` names; one approval covers the call, and the result lists each file's id and url, or why it was not uploaded. A CSV, Markdown, JSON or plain-text file, a symbolic or hard link, and a file outside the working directory each go in a call of their own with `file_path`.

favicon.description: Deprecated; Claude omits it and uses `icon`.

icon.description: One short generic word for the artifact's browser-tab icon, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map: a plain signifier, never a product or brand name. Claude includes it on every page's first publish and omits it on a redeploy so the artifact keeps its icon, passing a new one only when the person asks.

files.description: Supporting files to publish alongside the page, as a map {"published/path": "source/path" | {from, contentType} | null}. The key is what the HTML references. The source is a path on disk, or {from, contentType} when the type cannot be inferred from the published extension. null removes that path on an update, and files left out are kept. A plain list publishes each file at its own spelling. Sources must be under the working directory or Claude's scratchpad directory. `preflight.js` at the artifact root is reserved: it runs against open pages when Claude publishes updates, and it must be a JavaScript module of at most 8 KiB whose default export is a function, or the publish is refused.

path.description: Path relative to the working directory (or to `root`, which may be a folder in your scratchpad directory); the file is served at this same path next to the page.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the extension for common types (css/js/json/png/…) — pass explicitly otherwise.

from.description: Source file path — relative to `root` (default: the working directory), or absolute under the working directory or your scratchpad directory.

contentType.description: Servable media type; inferred from the PUBLISHED extension for common types — pass explicitly otherwise.

root.description: The base directory that relative `files` sources resolve against, like a bundler root. It never changes published paths. It is relative to the working directory, or absolute within it or within Claude's scratchpad directory. It requires `files`.

pin.description: publish only: true also pins the published artifact to the person's claude.ai sidebar once it is published. Claude passes it only when the person asked for that. A failed pin never fails the publish, and the result says so.

limit.description: list only: the maximum number of artifacts to return (default 25).

scope.description: list: which listing to return. 'mine' is the default. The others are 'shared', 'all', 'files' (with `url`) and 'assets' (with `url`, continued with `after`). See **Calls**.

title.description: publish: the fallback title for an HTML page whose file has no <title>. It is a name, not a summary, and Claude keeps it the same across redeploys.

description.description: publish: one sentence for the subtitle on the gallery card.

label.description: A short name for this publish, at most 60 characters (e.g. "Draft to legal"). Optional. It is a few words, not a description.

overwrite_unread.description: publish with `files` or `root` to an existing artifact: published paths this call may replace or remove although you have not read or listed them in this session. Every other path the call touches must be one you read by its `path`, saw in a file listing, or published yourself, and must not have changed since — otherwise nothing is sent and the refusal names each path. Name a path here only when the user asked for it to be replaced without looking at what is there; it never excuses a path that changed after you read it.

url.description: An existing artifact's claude.ai link (claude.ai/artifact/{id} or claude.ai/code/artifact/{uuid}); a chat, project or session link is not one, and `action: "list"` lists the person's artifacts. On a publish, it is the artifact to update in place, one the person owns or was given edit access to (a read of it says "writer"). Before publishing to an artifact this conversation has neither read nor published, Claude reads it (`action: "read"`) and builds on what comes back; a publish sent without that read is refused. A refusal that hands Claude the live version counts as that read: Claude merges its changes into that version and publishes the result, and never resends the refused content unchanged. Claude omits `url` for a new artifact or to redeploy a file this conversation already published. For read, delete and the other calls that take a URL, it is the artifact to act on.

prompt.description: read, for an artifact shared with the person: what Claude needs from it, which steers the isolated summary.

force.description: publish: a last-resort overwrite that **discards** the newer published version. On a conflict, Claude merges its changes onto the newer content that the rejection hands it and publishes again. Claude passes true only when the person explicitly said to discard that specific version, and the server may still refuse it over a version saved from inside the page.

out_dir.description: read with `path`: the directory to save into. The default is this artifact's folder in Claude's scratchpad directory, where saving needs no approval. A published file lands at <out_dir>/<published path>, and saving it outside that default folder asks the person first. An asset's file is named by its id plus its type's extension; saving it outside the default folder is an ordinary file save the person may be asked to approve.

path.description: read: the file's published path inside the artifact, exactly as a 'files' listing printed it ("index.html" is the page itself). The file is saved locally, the result says where, and a small text file's contents are included. It can instead be an uploaded asset's id (32 hex characters, from an 'assets' listing or an upload result), and that asset is saved to a local file. delete: the id of the one asset to remove.

paths.description: read: several published paths in place of `path`, up to 256 in one call. Each file is saved as a single `path` would be, and the result lists where each one landed, or why it could not be read, with small text files' contents included while they fit.

after.description: list with scope 'assets' only: the `next` value from a previous listing, passed to continue it.

capabilities.description: publish: the runtime capabilities this page declares, as {name: config}. Claude loads the `artifact-capabilities` skill before passing it. On a redeploy Claude omits the field to keep what the page has, and {} clears it.

contract.description: publish: the artifact's runtime version. Leaving it out keeps the current version (the default), 'latest' upgrades, and an exact version pins or rolls back. It changes how the published page behaves, so Claude passes it only when the author explicitly intends that change.

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Working directory persists between calls, but prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- IMPORTANT: Avoid using this tool to run `cat`, `head`, `tail`, `sed`, `awk`, or `echo` commands, unless explicitly instructed or after you have verified that a dedicated tool cannot accomplish your task. Instead, use the appropriate dedicated tool as this will provide a much better experience for the user.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__dismiss_task
tools.description:
Withdraw a background-task chip you previously created with spawn_task.

Call this when a suggestion you flagged is now stale, superseded, or irrelevant — e.g. you (or the user) already fixed it in this session, or you spawned a better-scoped replacement. To replace a chip: call spawn_task with the new suggestion first, then dismiss the old task_id.

Only chips the user hasn't acted on can be withdrawn from the queue. If the user already started or dismissed the task, the result says so (a dismissed task's copy kept for later is withdrawn too) — do not retry.

tools.description:
Mark the start of a new chapter in this session.

Call this when the work shifts to a meaningfully different phase — e.g. after finishing exploration and starting implementation, after a fix lands and you move to verification, or when the user pivots to an unrelated request. The user sees a divider in the transcript and a floating table of contents for jumping between chapters.

Use sparingly: a chapter should cover a coherent stretch of work, not every tool call. A typical session has 3–8 chapters. Do not mark a chapter for the very first message — the session start is implicit.

The title is a short noun phrase ("Codebase exploration", "Auth bug fix", "Test verification"), not a sentence.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_session__spawn_task
tools.description:
Flag an out-of-scope issue for a separate background task.

Call this when you notice something worth fixing that would bloat the current change — dead code, stale docs, missing coverage, a confirmed TODO, or a security issue spotted in passing. Don't flag vague code-smell observations, trivial fixes you can do inline, or low-confidence hunches. A chip appears for the user; one click spins it off into its own session. Your current turn continues uninterrupted.

The prompt must stand alone — include file paths and enough context to act without this conversation.

The result includes a task_id; call dismiss_task with it if the suggestion later becomes stale.

# FULL HANDOFF: Nxeon + Cyrus (written 2026-10-13 for a second Claude session on the primary server)

You are joining an ongoing project run by the owner (email haxkodi@gmail.com; also uses nicholas.sj.albanese@gmail.com as the Cyrus preview/test account). Read this whole file, then `memory/MEMORY.md`, then `agent-notes/cyrus-research/CYRUS-TRACKER.md` (91 numbered sections; sections 51-66 are the most recent). Everything below was verified on 2026-10-13 unless marked (U).

## 0. Owner preferences and standing rules (non-negotiable)
- Be concise. The owner is credit-limited: do not launch agents or long jobs unprompted; no paid third-party spend (baz, API tools) without sign-off.
- Model rule: Sonnet for research/small items, Opus only for big advanced features, few agents at a time. Never fabricate results; report failures plainly.
- Ask before: production deploys beyond what the owner already authorised, rotating live credentials, replying to support tickets (never without explicit sign-off), anything outward-facing. The auto-mode classifier blocks production deploys, feature-flag writes and secret/data export; do NOT work around a denial: stop and tell the owner (they can approve or exit auto mode).
- WARN, DON'T BLOCK: Cyrus must not hard-cap user choices; show warnings. Only security, legal, money/credit integrity and crash-safe type limits stay hard (memory: nxeon-cyrus-warn-dont-block).
- Never: `git add -A` in a worktree with symlinks (stage explicit paths); `pkill -f` (kill by PID/unit); edit/build inside /opt/nxeon or /opt/nxeon-staging; reuse VM IDs; run role/ownership SQL; put secrets in repos/docs; touch customer servers or VM 88001 from agents.
- Brand voice: never imply a third-party infrastructure provider exists to customers. "47 seconds" tagline is intentional. Update notes only with customer-facing changes.

## 1. Infrastructure map
- **Primary node** `ns5002569` (51.79.162.96, OVH Singapore): runs production. Prod app tree `/opt/nxeon` (NEVER edit/build there; only `git merge --ff-only` into main happens here, then promote). Postgres local (DATABASE_URL in `/opt/nxeon/.env`; never print it). Services: `nxeon-web`, `nxeon-worker` (systemd), nginx (`/etc/nginx/sites-enabled/{nxeon-cloud,cyrus-my,...}`, `conf.d/cloudflare-realip.conf`). ZFS pools: `data` (NVMe, customer VMs), `tank` (single 3.6 TB HDD, NO redundancy: backups, worktrees, uploads, packs). Root disk is small (~11 GB free): never fill it with caches.
- **node-2** (Hetzner FSN, root@178.63.94.114): BUILD HOST. All agent/dev heavy work goes through `/opt/nxeon/scripts/devhost` (run/test/tsc/build/db push; throwaway DB; `--lock` serialises). Production builds also run there via promote. Rules: `agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md`. Has JDK for Paper test flights (reuse `tools/testflight` harness).
- **VM 88001** (10.20.1.253, reached `ssh -J root@178.63.94.114 root@10.20.1.253`): Cyrus BUILD SERVICE (Docker image `modbuilder:0.9`, `/opt/modbuilder`, per-build workspace `/var/lib/modbuilder/data/builds/<buildId>/ws`). It runs the Claude CLI with the OWNER'S SUBSCRIPTION LOGIN (must become an API key before any public launch). Deploy with `TAG=modbuilder:X.Y bash scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh` (refuses if a build is running, auto-rollback, guard smoke test; backup `/opt/modbuilder/.backup-*.tgz`). Only the parent/owner deploys, never agents.
- **node-7**: hosts the owner's test Minecraft server `minecraft-f3izjh` (Paper 1.21.11). **Other nodes**: see memory (node-4 OVH game firewall note, node-5 etc.).
- **Domains/Cloudflare**: `nxeon.cloud` (zone 3d489bbbf1592b8aa3476880ba589659): Cloudflare DNS but NOT proxied (owner parked the proxy; prepared: SSL Full-strict, min TLS 1.2, nginx real-IP). Reason: Free plan caps uploads at 100 MB and requests at ~100 s (portal accepts 250 MB uploads, some actions run up to 180 s). `cyrus.my` (zone 474843c785f916483396b1935230a59a): PROXIED; serves a static landing page (`/var/www/cyrus.my`) and resource-pack hosting (`/packs/p/<sha1>.zip` from `/tank/cyrus-packs`). There is NO dashboard/login on cyrus.my yet (the app lives at nxeon.cloud/dashboard/cyrus; dual-host code exists but is unconfigured).
- **Tokens/credentials** (never commit plaintext): `/root/.secrets/cloudflare-cyrus.ini`, `cloudflare-nxeon.ini` (zone settings only), `cloudflare-nxeon-dns.ini` (DNS only), `claudeskills.pass` (passphrase of the encrypted copy in the repo). Owner should rotate the Cloudflare tokens eventually. Nxeon prod secrets live only in `/opt/nxeon/.env`.

## 2. Where Claude's knowledge lives (this is the shared workspace)
- GitHub: private repo `santino1233/claudeskills`, cloned at `/root/claudeskills`, auto-synced every 2 minutes by `claudeskills-sync` (systemd timer; script `/usr/local/bin/claudeskills-sync`; log `/var/log/claudeskills-sync.log`; deploy key `/root/.ssh/claudeskills_deploy`, ssh alias `github-claudeskills`). Whitelist: only small text (md/txt/json/sh/py/patch/yml) <1 MB; a guard blocks plaintext tokens; `secrets.tar.enc` is the AES-256 encrypted `/root/.secrets`.
- Symlinks into the repo: `/root/.claude/projects/-root/memory` -> `repo/memory` (index `MEMORY.md`, ~120 lines, one file per fact), `/root/.claude/skills` -> `repo/skills` (only `baz`), `/root/agent-notes` -> `repo/agent-notes`, `/root/CLAUDE.md` -> `repo/CLAUDE.md`. The owner's Windows PC syncs into `repo/local-pc/` (skills, settings, memory, scrubbed transcripts of the last 30 days).
- Two accounts: `claude-me` / `claude-friend` aliases in `/root/.bashrc` (`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/root/.claude` vs `/root/.claude-friend`; `join-second-account.sh` links skills+memory). Start both from `/root` so the memory path matches. Chat transcripts are NOT shared (local `/root/.claude/projects/-root/*.jsonl`, ~4.4 GB, contain pasted tokens). Coordinate through `agent-notes/HANDOFF.md` (who works on what/branch) and the tracker. One account per branch/worktree at a time.
- Notes: `agent-notes/cyrus-research/`: `CYRUS-TRACKER.md` (master state, update after every merge/incident), `CYRUS-FULL-PLAN.md`, `MASSIVE-MOD-TEST.md` ("The Gloam"), research reports BA..BL (BA reference mods, BB vanilla techniques, BC perf safety, BD GitHub mod-tools survey, BE testing+weapons, BF technique catalogue(+json), BG techniques integration, BI fresh ChunkMirror prompt, BJ token baseline, BK learning loop, BL token-savings plan + recipe-memory design), `GAPS-AND-IDEAS.md`, flight records `*-flights-2026-10-12.json`. Other notes: `agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md`, many older Nxeon notes.
- Repo docs (in `/opt/nxeon` git, read from a worktree): `docs/cyrus/` (numbered pages 00-14, `onboarding/PLAYBOOK.md` + `skills/` inventory + `games/`, `reference/*` generated, `config/`), `docs/CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md`, `docs/CYRUS-TEST-DEPLOY.md`, `docs/CYRUS-MOVE-RUNBOOK.md`, `docs/DOCUMENTATION.md`, third-party reference `docs/third-party/universal-modder` (on a branch). Private data (NOT git): `/tank/cyrus-knowledge/universal-modder` (74-game field notes), `/tank/cyrus-library-staging` (catalog + Modrinth reference mods + vanilla zips, private-only), `/tank/cyrus-library-incoming` (cloned skill repos, decompiles, JDK+Vineflower in `tools/`).

## 3. The two products
- **Nxeon**: the owner's VPS/game-server hosting business (Next.js app, worker, Proxmox nodes, Stripe, wallet, partner program, marketing site, free-Minecraft tier, Kodely partner). Many memory files cover it (see MEMORY.md).
- **Cyrus**: AI game-mod studio (Minecraft first; Hytale/FiveM ON HOLD). Pipeline: portal (Next.js inside the Nxeon app, `lib/cyrus/*`, `app/api/cyrus|mod-builder`) -> `createModBuild` -> **plan screen** (planner `lib/cyrus/planner`, capability catalogue per game/version `lib/cyrus/adapters/*capabilities*`, perf-risk classifier, lanes) -> **build service** on VM 88001 (`services/modbuilder/*`: intake guard (Haiku), router/tier (Katara=Haiku, Saka=Sonnet 5, Yakko=Opus), prompts, version sheets (javap-verified), failure rules, autofix, designers, NxPerf perf layer, repair loop) -> jar/pack -> **Test Flight gate** (real Paper boot, stress bot, mutants) -> **delivery orchestrator** (journal/rollback; Pack Loader plugin + server-sent resource pack; BetterModel for creatures) -> install on the player's server. Tokens: `CyrusToken*` tables (reserve/spend/release ledger; "failed_free"), token amounts are placeholders pending owner decisions. Host seam (`lib/cyrus/host`) keeps Cyrus separable from Nxeon; ratchet tests enforce it (`cyrusDb` accessor for Cyrus tables).
- Legal/privacy rules: community library contribution is automatic but CC0-only assets, never game-derived/third-party/imported code; vanilla Minecraft zips and the Modrinth corpus are private reference only (never served, never in git); learn only anonymized OUTCOME data by default, never user mod code; template sharing is separate opt-in; GPL/ARR code is never copied.

## 4. Deploy and git procedures
- Code flow: work in a git worktree under `/tank/dev-worktrees/<name>` (branch off `main`), heavy commands via `devhost`, commit with explicit paths + the attribution trailer the harness gives, then (owner-authorised) `cd /opt/nxeon && git merge --ff-only <branch>` and `bash scripts/promote-production.sh --skip-staging-check` (builds on node-2, schema push additive, smoke-tests on :3095, blue/green swap, auto-rollback; ~15-20 min; rollback `scripts/rollback-release.sh --production`). Never build in the live tree; classifier may block promotes in auto mode.
- Build-service changes (anything under `services/modbuilder`) only take effect after the image redeploy (see VM 88001). Web changes need a promote. Env flags: append to `/opt/nxeon/.env` (back it up first) + `systemctl restart nxeon-worker nxeon-web`; build-service knobs go in `/root/modbuilder.env` on VM 88001 then rerun `run.sh` when idle.
- Tests: `devhost test <files>` (node:test via tsx), `devhost tsc` (7 GB heap), `devhost db push` before `devhost build`. Docs reference pages are generated: `devhost run -- npx tsx scripts/cyrus/docs-build.ts` then copy `docs/cyrus/reference/*` back. Docs-coverage test fails on new flags/env/tests/links until regenerated.

## 5. Where things stand (2026-10-13)
**Live in production (preview account only; all public switches OFF):** `main` = `6204e045ef` in `/opt/nxeon`; live WEB release `20261012T071604Z-976bff15-...` (rc2 + intake router fix); build service image `modbuilder:0.9` (guard prompt fix, blank-final autofix, own compile-repair budget, NxPerf.queue prompt fix). Flags ON in prod env: CYRUS_DESIGNER, CYRUS_ITEM_STATES, CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_GATE, CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_BLOCK_ON_FAIL, CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL, CYRUS_DELIVERY, CYRUS_CONFIG_STUDIO, CYRUS_CREATURES. Launch pair `cyrus_studio_public_enabled` + `cyrus_tok_live` = false. Storage tables exist (CYRUS_STORAGE off). Backups: `/tank/backup/manual/nxeon-pre-rc2-20261011-2134.sql.gz`.
**Built, NOT merged/deployed (branches ahead of main; each has a report):**
- `feature/cyrus-mc-testing-weapons` +7 (602b831d86): survival combat bot, worldgen probes, harness mutants, failure rules, hitscan/beam/area_blast components. Report BE.
- `feature/cyrus-mc-techniques` +13 (88c0206f22, builds on the above): javap-verified API facts, vein miner, capture mob, combat tag/per-player fx recipes, armor + note-block lanes, technique eval set. Report BG. Flags: CYRUS_MC_TECHNIQUES (+MB_MC_TECHNIQUES), CYRUS_ARMOR_LANE, CYRUS_NOTEBLOCK_LANE, all OFF. 10 uncommitted files in `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-mc-tech` (the agent was cut off by the weekly rate limit; check `git status`).
- `feature/cyrus-prompt-coach` +7 (848da95f09): plan-screen prompt coach (flag CYRUS_PROMPT_COACH off; needs `prisma/manual-migrations/2026-10-12-cyrus-coach-events.sql` and `coach.js` in the next image).
- `feature/cyrus-learning-loop` +5 (09a5b3b663): outcome signals, token report (BJ), mining job -> candidate rules (never auto-applied), release manifest, admin stub (CYRUS_LEARNING off).
- `feature/cyrus-config-delivery` +6 (b5185109d5): Config Studio "Send to server" (was unwired/501 in prod). Real flight 19/19; uses a local soft check `lib/cyrus/delivery/config-check.ts` to reconcile with warn-don't-block.
- `feature/cyrus-skills-universal-modder` +3 (063571dbf0): skills inventory, vendored universal-modder (MIT) in `docs/third-party`, 29 per-game tool pages (`docs/cyrus/onboarding/skills/games`), Minecraft findings.
- `feature/cyrus-warn-dont-block`: agent died before committing; **68 uncommitted files** in `/tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-softlimits` (head = main's 976bff15d3). Unreviewed; finish or redo.
- Unmerged queued chips (spawn_task, one-click in the Claude app): `fix/cyrus-version-bump` (version resets to 1.0.0 on change builds), `fix/cyrus-change-regression-guards` (planner must not enable new generative lanes on change builds, additive designer compile, regression guard vs base build, router floor Saka for change builds).
- Older Cyrus branches `feature/cyrus-r0..r51`, `release/cyrus-rc1/rc2`, `feature/cyrus-modbuilder`, `feature/cyrus-perf-safety`, `feature/cyrus-mc-coverage` mostly merged into main via rc1/rc2; check with `git rev-list --count main..<branch>` before assuming.
**Known live problems / lessons (recent):** (1) ChunkMirror saga: planner read "mob spawner" as the Item designer lane and replaced a good mod (tracker 58b); good base build is mbc0fb90e7 (v1.3.0). (2) Troll build failed: shared repair counter + NxPerf field-initializer trap (fixed in image 0.9, tracker 66). (3) Intake guard + router false positives (fixed). (4) Plan-screen estimates run low (20/25 builds exceeded the shown range; Saka still on Sonnet 5, 9-10 turns vs 2-3 on 5.5). (5) Creature lane never proven end to end on a real client. (6) cyrus.my dashboard not wired. (7) Config studio values above old caps were clamped in generated plugins (warn-don't-block work pending).

#!/bin/bash
# (Re)create the Mod Builder container on the build VM. Idempotent.
#   AUTH, one source of truth. Preferred: ONE Claude login session file (what `claude login` writes to
#   ~/.claude/.credentials.json: access token + refresh token). Keep it in a dedicated directory,
#   CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS_DIR (default /root/.claude-modbuilder), created once with
#     CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR=/root/.claude-modbuilder claude login
#   (or copy an existing .credentials.json into it). The directory is mounted read-write at /run/claude-auth (CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR),
#   outside the CLI user's home and denied to the model's tools, so token refreshes persist and nothing else shares that login. When that file exists the
#   CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN line in claudebox.env is ignored (an env token would override the file).
#   WHERE TO EDIT (on the VM): /root/claudebox.env, one KEY=VALUE per line. Any ONE of: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (subscription),
#   ANTHROPIC_API_KEY (paid API), ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN (gateway bearer). Optional gateway: ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=https://host/v1,
#   EXTRA_ALLOWED_DOMAINS=host (the container firewall blocks everything else), MB_MODEL_PREFIX=cc/ (if the gateway namespaces models).
#   Then run this script again to restart the container.
#   Fallback (old way): /root/claudebox.env   CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=... (owner subscription)  -- or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... for paid API
#   /root/modbuilder.env  MODBUILDER_API_KEY=...      (bearer key the portal uses)
set -euo pipefail
IMAGE="${1:-modbuilder:0.5}"
# Routing / knowledge knobs (see route.js, prompts.js): passed through when set in the caller's env,
# e.g. MB_ROUTING=off /opt/modbuilder/run.sh modbuilder:0.3  (or put them in /root/modbuilder.env).
PASS=()
for k in MB_ROUTING MB_CLASSIFIER MB_MODEL_SIMPLE MB_MODEL_STANDARD MB_MODEL_COMPLEX MB_REPAIR_MODEL MB_REPAIR_CHEAP_MODEL MB_REPAIR_CHEAP_FIRST MB_REPAIR_SMALL_MAX MB_ROUTE_SIMPLE_MAX MB_ROUTE_COMPLEX_MIN MB_SHEETS MB_RULES MB_MAX_REPAIRS MB_LIVE_STREAM MB_MAX_TURNS MB_MAX_TURNS_REPAIR MB_AUTOFIX MB_LEAN_TOOLS MB_EFFORT MB_CACHE_TTL MB_DEDUPE MB_DEDUPE_MAX_AGE_H MB_TIER_KATARA MB_TIER_SAKA MB_TIER_YAKKO MB_STARTER_BANK MB_RECIPES MB_RECIPES_HOLDBACK_PCT; do
  if [[ -n "${!k:-}" ]]; then PASS+=(-e "$k=${!k}"); fi
done
CRED_DIR="${CLAUDE_CREDENTIALS_DIR:-/root/.claude-modbuilder}"
# Credentials files: defaults are the Nxeon VM layout; override to relocate the service (the entrypoint reads the same env-file).
CLAUDEBOX_ENV="${CLAUDEBOX_ENV:-/root/claudebox.env}"
MODBUILDER_ENV="${MODBUILDER_ENV:-/root/modbuilder.env}"
ENVFILE="$CLAUDEBOX_ENV"
CRED_MOUNT=()
if [[ -f "$CRED_DIR/.credentials.json" ]]; then
  CUID="$(docker run --rm --entrypoint id "$IMAGE" -u claude)"
  chown -R "$CUID:$CUID" "$CRED_DIR"; chmod 700 "$CRED_DIR"; chmod 600 "$CRED_DIR/.credentials.json"

#!/bin/bash
# =============================================================================
# devhost — run agent dev work on the BUILD HOST (node-2), not on the primary.
#
# Edit files on the primary as usual (your own git worktree — never /opt/nxeon),
# then run every heavy command through this helper. It mirrors your worktree's
# source to node-2 (/tank/nxeon-build/wt/<name>, own node_modules there), runs the
# command inside the capped nxeon-build-agents.slice with a THROWAWAY database
# (Postgres on node-2 127.0.0.1:5433), and streams the output back.
#
#   scripts/devhost run [--lock] [--max SEC] -- CMD...   push + run CMD in the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost tsc                                  = run -- npx tsc --noEmit
#   scripts/devhost test [FILES...]                      = run --lock -- npx tsx --test ...
#   scripts/devhost build                                = run --lock -- npx next build
#   scripts/devhost dev [--port P]                       start `next dev` on node-2 (background unit)
#   scripts/devhost bg NAME [--port P] -- CMD...         any background process (worker, preview server)
#   scripts/devhost stop [NAME|all]                      stop this worktree's background units
#   scripts/devhost logs [NAME] [-n N] [-f]              journal of a background unit (default: dev)
#   scripts/devhost tunnel PORT [LOCAL_PORT]             ssh -L so the primary can curl/Playwright it
#   scripts/devhost pull REMOTE_PATH [LOCAL_DEST]        copy results (screenshots, reports) back
#   scripts/devhost push                                 just sync files (run does this itself)
#   scripts/devhost install                              force npm install + prisma generate there
#   scripts/devhost db push|reset|info                   throwaway DB: schema push / recreate / name
#   scripts/devhost env set KEY=VALUE | unset KEY | list extra env for this worktree (never prod secrets)
#   scripts/devhost rm                                   stop units, drop the throwaway DB, delete the node-2 copy
#   scripts/devhost ls | status | sync                   workspaces / node-2 load / push refs to node-2's mirror
#
# Rules: /root/agent-notes/BUILD-HOST.md. The node-2 copy is a build/run sandbox,
# not a place to edit or commit — your primary-side worktree stays the source of truth.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail
HERE="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "$0")")"
# shellcheck source=lib/buildhost-env.sh
source "$HERE/lib/buildhost-env.sh"
REPO="${DEVHOST_REPO:-/opt/nxeon}"

die() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
say() { echo "devhost: $*" >&2; }
q() { printf '%q ' "$@"; }

# Nxeon — VPS hosting platform

Hostinger-style VPS hosting platform running on this Proxmox VE 9 dedicated server (OVH KS-GAME, i7-7700K, 64GB RAM, 2×450GB NVMe ZFS mirror + 4TB HDD backup pool).

## Architecture

- **Web panel**: Next.js 15 (App Router, server actions) + Tailwind v4, served by `nxeon-web.service` on port 3000, behind nginx on port 80. Public IP: 51.79.162.96.
- **Worker**: `worker/index.ts` run by `nxeon-worker.service` (as root — it manages iptables). Polls the `Job` table every 3s and executes provisioning/lifecycle jobs against the Proxmox API.
- **DB**: PostgreSQL 17, database `nxeon`, Prisma ORM ([prisma/schema.prisma](prisma/schema.prisma)). Use `npm run db:push` after schema changes.
- **Proxmox**: API token auth (`nxeon@pve!platform`, creds in `.env`). Templates: VMID 9000 (Ubuntu 24.04), 9001 (Debian 13), cloud-init based, cloned onto ZFS storage `vmdata`.
- **Networking**: VMs attach to NAT bridge `vmbr1` (10.20.0.0/24, gateway .1). IPs allocated from 10.20.0.100–250 ([lib/ipam.ts](lib/ipam.ts)). SSH exposed via DNAT port forwards 20000–29999 in iptables chain `NXEON_FWD`, rebuilt from DB by [worker/network.ts](worker/network.ts) — never edit that chain by hand.
- **Cloud-init**: vendor snippet at `/tank/backup/snippets/nxeon-vendor.yaml` (installs qemu-guest-agent, enables root password SSH).

## Portals & design system

**As of 2026-09-14, the customer portal is the "Nexion" redesign** — previously developed in isolation on a separate box (node-2, `/opt/nxeon-v2`, branch `design/v2`) and merged into `main` once it was fully audited and verified. Read this section before touching any shared styling — it is the difference between an edit that stays contained and one that silently reaches marketing, login, or admin.

- **Two portals, two shells, deliberately unmerged:**
  - `app/admin/**` (admin ops portal) still renders through `components/portal/Shell.tsx` — the ORIGINAL, pre-redesign chrome. Marketing (`app/(marketing)/**`), `/login`, `/register` and admin must stay pixel-identical to how they looked before the redesign. Never edit these expecting Nexion's visual language to apply, and never move Nexion-only styling into a place they can see it.
  - `app/dashboard/**` (customer portal) renders through `components/nx/Shell.tsx` — the Nexion redesign. This is where the new design system, its components (`components/nx/*`), and its color/animation language live.
  - **A component added to one shell must be added to the other if it's meant to exist on both.** This has silently broken things before: `ComposeProvider`, `TerminalDockProvider`, `MatrixProvider` were each added to `components/portal/Shell.tsx` first and forgotten on `components/nx/Shell.tsx`, taking a whole feature down invisibly (the crash only appeared on a route a smoke test didn't walk).

- **The scoping trick that keeps the two visually separate — `app/globals.css`, `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)`:**
  Nexion's own colors/tokens and its overrides of shared component classes (`.card`, `.btn-primary`, `.input`, etc.) are NOT bare rules — they're wrapped in `:root:has(.nx-shell-root) { ... }`, a selector that only matches when a `.nx-shell-root` element (rendered only by `components/nx/Shell.tsx`) exists anywhere on the page. That's the entire mechanism keeping marketing/login/admin rendering their original, pre-redesign styles: **do not write a new bare rule for a class both portals share** (e.g. a bare `.card { ... }` outside this scope) — it will apply everywhere, including where it was never meant to.
  - Light mode has its own nested scope for the same reason: `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)[data-theme="light"]`, NOT a bare `html[data-theme="light"]`. The bare form loses a CSS specificity fight to the dark `:has()` block regardless of which theme is active — this was a real, session-spanning bug (several "light mode doesn't work on page X" reports all had this one root cause) before it was scoped correctly.
  - `.nx-dark-island` is a third scope, deliberately staying dark inside the Nexion portal even when light mode is active (site headers, page hero banners) — it re-declares the relevant tokens back to dark values inside `html[data-theme="light"] .nx-dark-island { ... }`. Add a new always-dark token here too if you introduce one (see `--color-neon-bug` for the pattern: declared in the base `@theme` block, overridden lighter in the light-mode scope, re-declared back to its bright value inside `.nx-dark-island`).

- **CSS/JS landmines hit (and fixed) building this — avoid repeating them:**
  - **`@keyframes` and `@property` are not valid nested inside a plain style rule** — only inside `@layer`/`@media`/other at-rules. Nesting one inside `:root:has(...) { }` (or any class selector) silently drops it at build time — no error, the animation just never plays, forever, with every other signal (computed `animation-name`, `animation-play-state: running`) looking correct. This broke ~34 animations at once (a levitating icon, the page preloader, several status dots) when a broad `:has()` refactor accidentally wrapped them. If an animation looks "stuck on frame one," check whether its `@keyframes` block ended up nested inside a style rule.
  - **`backdrop-filter` on an ancestor creates a new containing block for `position: fixed` descendants.** A `.card` with `backdrop-blur-md` breaks any non-portaled modal/overlay nested inside it (it pins to the card instead of the viewport). Fix: cancel the inherited `backdrop-filter` on the offending class, or `createPortal` the fixed element to `document.body`.
  - **A positioned `fixed; z-0` decorative background (an aurora/globe effect) paints above ordinary static content** unless the real content wrapper gets `relative z-[1]`.
  - **Hydration-mismatch anti-pattern**: `useState(() => { if (typeof window === "undefined") return X; ...read window/URL...; return Y; })` — the server always takes the `X` branch, the client's first render always takes `Y`, guaranteed mismatch. Read the value server-side (a Server Component's `searchParams` prop) and pass it down as a real prop instead.
  - Percentage-based `transform: translateY(%)` inside a flex item whose container has no defined width/height resolves against 0 and silently does nothing — give the container a real dimension (e.g. `inset-0` instead of `inset-y-0 right-0` alone) before debugging the animation itself.
  - `git commit -m` with backticks in the message breaks — write the message to a file and use `git commit -F`.
  - Bash `cwd` does not persist between tool calls in an agent session — always `cd /opt/nxeon && ...` in the same command.

- Design system tokens/classes live in `app/globals.css` + `components/ui/primitives.tsx` (shared/production) and `components/nx/*` (Nexion-only). Charts are dependency-free SVG (`components/ui/charts.tsx`) — do not add a charting library.

- Always `git commit` working states; never leave the tree broken — services restart from this directory.

content.content:
## 3. Rebuild the build-service image on VM 88001

This step is independent of the site. The new image is backwards compatible: the portal sends nothing new while the switches are off.

**Script:** `scripts/cyrus/deploy-modbuilder.sh`. `/root/agent-notes/deploy-modbuilder.sh` is now a wrapper around it; set `REPO=` to the merged tree. Run it with `--list` first to see the file list.

**What gets copied.** Every file the Dockerfile copies, derived from the Dockerfile itself and guarded by `test/modbuilder-dockerfile.test.ts`:

- 25 service modules: `server`, `scan`, `prompts`, `route`, `precheck`, `live`, `usage`, `autofix`, `jar`, `import`, `textures`, `sound-spec`, `sounds`, `creature-spec`, `creatures`, `capabilities`, `datapack-spec`, `datapacks`, `designer-spec`, `designs`, `itemmodels`, `itemmodel-spec`, `release`, `catalog`, `catalog-mcp` (all `.js`).
- Data files: `texture-example.json`, `sound-example.json`, `sound-catalog.json`, `sound-catalog.txt`, `datapack-example.json`, `worldgen-example.json`, `creature-example.json`, `designer-example.json`, `designer-gameplay-example.json`, `designer-boss-example.json`, `designer-hud-example.json`, `itemmodel-example.json`.
- Directories: `template/`, `sheets/`, `rules/`.
- Other files: `tools/gen-classpath-26.sh`, `tools/fetch-import-deps.js`, `entrypoint.sh`, `package.json`, `run.sh`, `Dockerfile`.
- From `lib/`: `lib/cyrus/versions/registry.json` and `lib/cyrus/import/deps.json`.
- `toolchain.tgz` must already be in `/opt/modbuilder` on the VM. The script checks for it.

**The old hand-kept script was missing** 9 modules, 6 data files and `template/`. The image build would have failed, or silently used stale copies.

**JDK 25 / 26.x lane.** Run with `JDK25=yes`. That adds the pinned Temurin `25.0.4.1+1` and Gradle `9.8.1` build arguments, each sha256-verified, plus `MC26_PINS='26.2=26.2.build.133-stable 26.1.2=26.1.2.build.74-stable'`.

- Resolving the 26.x classpath does NOT make 26.x buildable. That is the registry's `buildable` flag (today `false` for 26.1.2, 26.2 and 26.3).
- Mark a 26.x version buildable only after this image is live and an eval has run.

**Health checks the script makes.**

- Before: the service is idle (`running:0`), and it records the running image tag for rollback.
- After:
  - `promptVersion` equals `prompts.js`.
  - `features.catalogTools:true` confirms the new image is the one running.
  - `release.scannerSha256` equals the sha256 of `scan.js`, so the hardened scan is live. On a mismatch the script rolls back.
  - `release.registrySha256` equals `registry.json`.
  - The `auth` field: `api_key` for a paid key; `subscription` or `subscription_login` for your login; `gateway_token`; or `none`. Before r28, the login-file mode wrongly reported `none`.

**Smoke.** The script sends one injection-style request that the guard must refuse (`errorCode: refused`). That is one Haiku guard call.

Afterwards, run `smoke-readonly.sh service`.

**Rollback.** Automatic on a failed build or health check. By hand:

```
ssh -J root@178.63.94.114 root@10.20.1.253 'cd /opt/modbuilder && tar xzf .backup-<ts>.tgz -C /opt/modbuilder && ./run.sh <previous image>'
```

The script prints the exact backup file name and the previous image.

## Env var reference (unset = default)

**Web**

- Feature switches, all default off: `CYRUS_DESIGNER`, `CYRUS_ITEM_STATES`, `CYRUS_DATAPACK_STUDIO`, `CYRUS_WORLDGEN`, `CYRUS_CREATURES`, `CYRUS_SOUND_LIBRARY_CLEARED`, `CYRUS_TESTFLIGHT_BLOCK_ON_FAIL`, `CYRUS_CATALOG_TOOLS`.
- Wiring 2 (routes 404 while off): `CYRUS_DELIVERY`, plus the part switches for the preview (`CYRUS_MANAGED_PLUGINS_REAL`, `CYRUS_DATAPACK_DELIVERY_REAL`); `CYRUS_MODPACKS`; `CYRUS_SERVER_DOCTOR`; `CYRUS_HEALTH_TELEMETRY` + `CYRUS_HEALTH_TELEMETRY_SECRET`; `CYRUS_MESHGEN`, `CYRUS_MESHGEN_SCRATCH`, `CYRUS_MESHGEN_QUEUE_DIR` (default `NXEON_MODBUILD_DIR/meshgen`).
- `CYRUS_CATALOG_INDEX`: unset, so no catalog offer.
- `CYRUS_SOUND_RENDER`: off; set `relay` on the web. With it, `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_URL` and `CYRUS_SOUND_RELAY_TOKEN`.
- Pack store:
  - `CYRUS_PACK_STORE`: off in production.
  - `CYRUS_PACK_PUBLIC_BASE`
  - `CYRUS_PACK_MAX_BYTES`: 100 MB.
  - `CYRUS_PACK_S3_*`
- `CYRUS_MODEL_PREVIEW`: off. It is refused in production; Chromium previews run only on node-2.
- `MODBUILDER_URL` and `MODBUILDER_API_KEY`, or `MODBUILDER_ENV_FILE` (default `/etc/nxeon/modbuilder.env`).

**Worker**
| `NXEON_MODBUILD_DIR` | `/var/lib/nxeon/modbuilds` |

**Build service (VM, in `/root/modbuilder.env` or `/root/claudebox.env`; see `run.sh`)**

- `MODBUILDER_API_KEY`
- One login: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, or `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` + `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` + `EXTRA_ALLOWED_DOMAINS`, or the login file.
- Defaults:
  - `MB_MODEL`: sonnet
  - `MB_CONCURRENCY`: 2
  - `MB_BUILD_BUDGET_USD`: 4
  - `MB_CALL_BUDGET_USD`: 2.5
  - `MB_GUARD`: on
  - `MB_ROUTING`: on
- `cyrus_mods_public_enabled`
- `cyrus_passrate_enabled` (r33 pass-rate page)
- `cyrus_lifecycle_enabled`, `cyrus_compat_watch_enabled`
- `cyrus_meshgen_price_*` (read by the meshgen estimate since wiring 2; unset = a token-only estimate)

The keys outside `set-setting.sh`'s allow-list are set in `/admin/settings`, or through a one-line `psql` upsert like the one in `set-setting.sh`.

## r32 security hardening (deploy notes)
- New env `CYRUS_API_V1_IDENTITY_CLIENTS` (default `nxeon`): leave unset unless a second client must act for Nxeon accounts.
- Rebuild the build-service image (regenerated `designer-spec.js`, `config-spec.js`, `datapack-spec.js`; `tools/testflight/lib.js`); copy the updated meshgen files (`sbx-meshgen.sh`, `mg_harness.py`, `mg_scratch.py`) to node-2 with the meshgen worker.
- No migration. Open items before switching on telemetry, the AI gateway and meshgen scratch: `docs/CYRUS-SECURITY-AUDIT.md` (O-1, O-2, O-13).

## Verification jobs (no deploy needed, r33)

- **Eval run (paid, owner budget):** from a worktree, `npx tsx scripts/cyrus/eval-run.ts --dry-run --preset first-run` (free: plan + estimate), then `npx tsx scripts/cyrus/eval-run.ts --tag first1 --preset first-run --budget <USD> --testflight`. Interrupted? Run the same command again. Results in `/root/cyrus-eval/first1/` (`report.md`, `baseline.json`). Accept the run by copying `baseline.json` to `services/modbuilder/eval/baseline.json` and committing it; the pass-rate page shows only that file.
- **Real-client test day (free):** `scripts/cyrus/testday.sh build`, `fetch`, then per version `start <version> <your Minecraft name>`, follow `CHECKLIST.md`, `stop`; finally `ingest results.json --apply` and commit the `lib/cyrus/versions/` diff. Only that flips `resourcePackClientVerified`.
## r35 Minecraft completion (deploy notes, every switch OFF)
- **Legacy 1.21.1 textures**: switch on together, after the build-service image is rebuilt from this branch: `MB_LEGACY_TEXTURES=1` on the builder (VM 88001) and `CYRUS_LEGACY_TEXTURES=1` in the web process. One off = 1.21.1 textures stay off (as today). No migration.

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy the Cyrus build service (services/modbuilder) to the build VM 88001 and rebuild its image. OWNER RUNS THIS

## Build lock, memory and load
One heavy job at a time on node-2 (builds, `devhost test|build|run --lock`). Many agents queue; weekly model usage is the other limit. node-2's agent slice has OOM-killed `next dev` (5+ GB) several times: run screenshots in batches and restart. input.command:
cd /tank/dev-worktrees/cyrus-capacity && python3 - <<'EOF'
p="docs/cyrus/07-operations.md"; s=open(p).read()
a="## Observability and backups (r37, built, NOT installed)"
assert s.count(a)==1
new = '''## Build capacity (queue, priorities, limits; 2026-10-14, branch `feature/cyrus-capacity-queue`)
Why: on 2026-10-13/14 the owner's own build waited behind two eval builds on the one build VM (88001, `MB_CONCURRENCY=2`, container `--memory 5g`), and the subscription login hit its session limit while agents and evals ran, failing builds with `ai_unavailable` (tracker 103). Everything below is in the build-service image (`scheduler.js`, `capacity.js`) and the portal; defaults are the safe ones and `MB_PRIORITY=off` restores plain FIFO.

**Priority classes.** `interactive` (portal user builds; the default for any request that names no class, so older portals keep working), `batch` (eval runs, mining jobs, admin re-runs: explicit `priority: "batch"`, or the fallback by id prefix `ev-`/`eval-`/`eval_`/`mine-`/`batch-` or an `eval:` account; the eval runners send `priority: "batch"` themselves) and `system` (the deploy script's guard smoke). Order: class, then per-account fair share (the account with fewer builds running first, ties to the account served least recently = round robin), then FIFO. The portal sends an opaque account key (`u:` + 16 hex of a salted sha256 of the user id), never the id.

**Reservation.** Batch may run on at most `MB_CONCURRENCY - MB_RESERVE_INTERACTIVE` slots (default 2 - 1 = 1), so a user build always has a free slot within one build's time. The price at concurrency 2: an eval runs one build at a time (`queue-sim` shows the eval batch finishing later than with FIFO). The reserve is clamped to concurrency - 1; at `MB_CONCURRENCY=1` nothing can be reserved and `/health capacity.warnings` says so. **Starvation guard:** a batch build waiting `MB_BATCH_STARVE_MIN` (30) ranks ahead of new interactive work, on non-reserved slots only.

**Admission control (hard: capacity limits are not user choices).** `MB_QUEUE_MAX` (40) builds in line, `MB_QUEUE_MAX_BATCH` (30) of them batch, `MB_ACCOUNT_MAX_ACTIVE` (3, builder side, only for requests with an account) answer a retryable `503 capacity` / `429 account_busy` with `retryAfterSec` before anything is stored. The portal's own per-account cap is the setting `cyrus_capacity_account_max_active` (2, was the constant MAX_INFLIGHT) and its rate limits (3/min, 20/h) now return `code: rate_limited` + `retryAfterSec`. A refused build is marked `errorCode: capacity` with a calm message, its token hold is released and it is never charged (settle reason `failed_infra`, not counted against the free failures).

**AI limits (graceful degradation).** A session/rate-limit/overload answer (`capacity.js isAiLimit`) no longer fails the build: it goes back in line at its old place with the lost attempt moved aside (`lostCostUsd`, `lostAiCalls`; `costUsd`, which the portal charges, starts at 0 again) and retries by itself after a backoff (`MB_AI_RETRIES` 2, `MB_AI_BACKOFF_S` 60 doubling to `MB_AI_BACKOFF_MAX_S` 900). The **circuit breaker** opens on the limit: while open no NEW AI build starts (bank, designer edits, imports still run), after the backoff exactly one build probes, its answer closes it. So one limit hit costs a wait, not a failed queue. Out of retries = `ai_unavailable` with "The AI is busy right now and did not answer after N tries. Nothing is charged", and the portal settles it free.

**Honest waits.** `GET /builds/:id` carries `queue` while queued: `position` (the order the scheduler will really start them in, pinned by the load test), `ahead`, `state` (`next` / `waiting` / `ai_wait`), `waitSec.p50/p80` from the p50/p80 of the last 60 AI build run times (null until 5 builds finished: no number is shown then), `retryAt`. `/health capacity` adds running/queued per class, time-in-line and run-time percentiles, the breaker, the caps and `suggestedConcurrency`. Screens: the build pages say "Starting soon" (next, measured wait under 90 s), "Next in line", "Waiting for a free builder: N builds are ahead of yours; usually about X-Y min", or "Waiting for the AI ... tries again by itself ... nothing is charged" (`lib/cyrus/builder/queue-view.ts`); the plan screen adds one line about the builder's queue right now behind `CYRUS_CAPACITY_UI=1`. The old fixed text "Cyrus builds two mods at a time in the preview" is gone.

**Admin.** The Live tab shows a Build capacity panel per builder (slots and reserve, running and waiting by class, oldest waiting, time in line and run time p50/p80 with sample counts, breaker, the image's own warnings) with alerts at `cyrus_capacity_alert_queue_depth` (6) builds waiting and `cyrus_capacity_alert_wait_p80_min` (10). All three settings are PLACEHOLDER numbers pending the owner (Audit & settings, group Build capacity).

**How many builds can run (MB_CONCURRENCY).** `MB_CONCURRENCY=auto` derives it from the container: floor((memory - `MB_BASE_MB` 600) / `MB_PER_BUILD_MB` 1200), at most 2 per CPU, at least 1; `/health capacity.suggestedConcurrency` always reports it. Measured inputs:
- Build run time (evals first1 65 builds / second1 38 builds, journal `durationMs`): p50 164 s / 150 s, p80 297 s / 305 s, p95 396 s / 423 s, max 550 s. These are what the estimates will converge to.
- Per-build memory: NOT measured on the build VM (agents do not touch VM 88001, and `build.json` records no RSS). The 1200 MB per build is a PLACEHOLDER estimate: the Claude CLI (Node) holding a build session (~0.3-0.5 GB) plus javac against the Paper API at its peak (see the javac measurement below) plus slack; the service itself and idle tools are the 600 MB base. To measure, the owner runs on the VM during a busy hour: `docker stats --no-stream modbuilder` and `docker exec modbuilder ps -o rss,args -u claude`, then sets `MB_PER_BUILD_MB` to the peak per build x 1.25.
- Test Flight (real Paper boot) runs on node-2, not in the build container: `-Xmx` at most 1 GB, RSS cap 512-2048 MB per flight (`lib/cyrus/testflight/spec.ts`), inside node-2's build slices. It does not count against the build VM's memory.
- At the 5 GB container: auto gives 3. Raising `MB_CONCURRENCY` above 2 needs `MB_MEMORY` (run.sh `--memory`, default `5g`) raised to `base + N x per-build`, and the AI login's own concurrency limit in mind (the subscription limit is what failed on 2026-10-13; an API key raises it).

Load test (fakes, zero cost): `test/modbuilder-capacity.test.ts` (3 accounts x 5 builds + 10 batch through the real scheduler on a fake clock: interactive p80 better than the best FIFO wait, never more than 1 batch build running, round robin, no starvation, positions = real start order, exact estimates for equal builds) and `test/modbuilder-capacity-service.test.ts` (the real server.js with a fake CLI: reservation over HTTP, the batch line and account caps, a session-limit answer retried by itself and not charged). Distribution: `npx tsx scripts/cyrus/queue-sim.ts [--concurrency N --reserve N --fifo]`.

## Scale-out: more build workers (design + portal side built; no second VM exists)
- **Mode:** `CYRUS_MB_DISPATCH=1` + `MODBUILDER_URLS=http://127.0.0.1:7340,http://127.0.0.1:7341` (two or more, same `MODBUILDER_API_KEY`) in the portal env. Off or one URL = the single `MODBUILDER_URL`, exactly as before.
- **Stateless dispatcher** (`lib/cyrus/builder/dispatch.ts`): a NEW build goes to the healthy worker with the lowest (running + queued) / concurrency that serves its Minecraft version, avoiding a worker whose AI breaker is open; ties to the first listed. A CHANGE build goes to the worker that holds its base build (the base workspace lives there). Every later call for a build (status, live, source, artifact, cancel) goes to the worker that has it: an in-memory sticky map, and on a miss (restart, the other web process, the worker sweep) the dispatcher asks each worker `GET /builds/<id>` once. Build ids are global (`mb` + 20 hex), so no table is needed. `/health` answers are cached 5 s per worker; planner/coach calls go to the least-loaded worker.
- **What does not move:** builds stay on the worker they started on (a dead worker's builds fail after the 2-hour stale rule as today); the starter bank, rules, sheets and knobs must be the same image and env on every worker (the portal reads features from the first healthy one). Each worker has its own queue and fair share; the dispatcher balances between them by load.
- **Adding a VM:** docs only, owner runs it: [CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK "Add a second build VM"](../CYRUS-DEPLOY-RUNBOOK.md#add-a-second-build-vm-docs-only-owner-runs-it).

'''
s=s.replace(a,new+a)
open(p,"w").write(s)
EOF
echo done
input.description: Write build capacity and scale-out docs in 07

All five parts are done on `feature/cyrus-capacity-queue`. Nothing is deployed and no production or VM action was taken.

**Commits:** 1531d4c170 (build service), a2f2ce282a (portal + dispatcher), cba2c1aafb (load test + `queue-sim.ts`), 34edc0d745 (docs, refs regenerated and copied back). Parts 1+2 and 2-4 share commits because `server.js` and `client.ts` couldn't be split cleanly.

**Tests:** `devhost tsc` = 0. Full suite was 3637/3638; the one failure was a cyrus-coach pin on the plan route. I fixed it and the rerun of the affected files passed 185/185. The 3 accounts × 5 + 10 batch simulation: user p80 wait 1159 s vs at least 1326 s under FIFO, never more than one batch build running, round robin between accounts, no starvation.

**Defaults:** reserve 1 of 2 slots, builder-side account cap 3, line max 40 (batch 30), 2 AI retries with backoff from 60 s to 900 s. PLACEHOLDER: `cyrus_capacity_account_max_active`=2, alert at 6 waiting / p80 wait 10 min, `MB_PER_BUILD_MB`=1200.

**Deploy:** priorities, reservation, admission limits and AI retry need an image redeploy (tag 0.16). Queue wording, the never-charged rule, settings, Live panel and dispatcher need a portal promote.

**Owner enables:** nothing to set once deployed. Optional: `CYRUS_CAPACITY_UI=1` (plan-screen line), `CYRUS_MB_DISPATCH` + `MODBUILDER_URLS`.

**Unverified:** per-build memory on 88001 (agents don't touch it). javac peak was 160–232 MB on node-2. No real build or real limit hit on the new scheduler. Dispatcher only tested against fake workers. No browser screenshots. The `eval:` prefix is an account prefix; build ids can't contain ":" so eval ids use `ev-`.
